cands.name: Lois Frankel
cands.bio: Democrat; U.S. Rep. since 2013 (FL-22, FL-21, FL-22), now running in new FL-23. Former West Palm Beach mayor (2003-2011) and 14-year Florida House member, including first woman House Minority Leader. Won 2026 primary with about 74.7%.
cands.local_ties: Moved to West Palm Beach in 1974; new FL-23 covers parts of Broward and southern Palm Beach counties (Boca Raton, Coral Springs, most of Deerfield Beach and Fort Lauderdale per Wikipedia).

record.text: Appropriations Committee; Ranking Member of the State, Foreign Operations and Related Programs subcommittee; also sits on the Labor-HHS-Education subcommittee (119th Congress).
Lead House sponsor of the Global HER Act to permanently repeal the Mexico City policy; chaired the Democratic Women's Caucus 2019-2025.
Left the Congressional Progressive Caucus in 2023 after voting to censure Rep. Rashida Tlaib (per The Intercept, cited by Wikipedia).
Announced in May 2026 she would run in the new 23rd district after the mid-decade remap.

money_notes.text: Chairs the Elect Democratic Women PAC (per Wikipedia). AIPAC and Democratic Majority for Israel are listed among her endorsers (an endorsement, not a payment). No outside-spending figure for FL-23 was found.

controversies.text: During her 2012 campaign she accepted $20,000 from Digital Domain Media Group about five months after the company received a downtown West Palm Beach project with city incentives; per Wikipedia she vowed to give the money to charity.

endorsements.text: Labor and groups listed on Wikipedia's 2026 FL-23 section: AFGE, Florida AFL-CIO, UAW, NEA, AIPAC, Democratic Majority for Israel, Jewish Democratic Council of America, Planned Parenthood Action Fund, Sierra Club, Giffords.

cands.gaps: No FL-23 outside-spending or top-donor data found. Her state-legislature votes (FL House 1986-2000) not retrieved. Residence not stated in sources.

votes.what: Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.
Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

cands.name: Deborah Adeimy
cands.bio: Republican nominee in new FL-23. Financial advisor who ran for the old FL-22 in 2022 and 2024 (per Wikipedia's 2026 election page). Has not held public office. Won the Aug 18, 2026 GOP primary over Paola Branda, 73.7%-26.3% (Wikipedia results table).

record.text: No elected or appointed office found; financial advisor and repeat congressional candidate (2022, 2024, 2026).
FEC: statement of candidacy filed 06/04/2026 (committee 'Deborah Adeimy for Congress', C00791541).

money_notes.text: FEC page (coverage to 10/14/2026) shows the campaign funded partly by candidate contributions and candidate loans alongside individual contributions; no independent-expenditure totals were visible when I opened the page.

cands.gaps: No photo, campaign website, social accounts or endorsements verified; web-search budget ran out before a bio search. No votes (never held voting office).
